name: isst_daemon
prose: Precondition: debug_mode, poll_interval and no_daemon are the daemon options; poll_interval < 0 selects the HFI (out-of-band) mode. Postcondition (isst_daemon, isst-daemon.c:233-263; the slice shows only its tail and 'poll_loop' is not a function): unless no_daemon is set, debug_mode is off and poll_interval is negative (in which case it prints a notice and calls daemonize), it installs signal_handler for SIGINT; it then calls init_levels. With a negative poll_interval it calls hfi_main, prints 'HFI initialization failed' if that returned nonzero, always prints 'Must specify poll-interval', and returns hfi_main's result. Otherwise it prints a debug message and loops while the static flag done is zero, sleeping poll_interval seconds and calling poll_for_config_change each time; done is set only by signal_handler, which then calls hfi_exit() and exit(0), so the loop ends in practice by the process exiting, and the final 'return 0' is reached only if done is set without that exit.
note: slice cut the head; real function isst_daemon (the item 'poll_loop' is a loop excerpt). The old prose (never returns for another reason) ignored the HFI branch and the early return; done is only set in signal_handler (isst-daemon.c:138), which also exits.

name: format_and_print_txt
prose: Precondition: outf is a writable stream, level >= 0, header and value may each be NULL. Postcondition (format_and_print_txt, isst-display.c:84-109; returns void): if level is 0 it returns without writing anything and without touching the static delimiters buffer. For level 1 it sets delimiters to a single space; for level > 1 it fills delimiters with level-1 repetitions of two spaces using snprintf calls whose remaining-size argument is sizeof(delimiters) - j (the text is cut at the 256-byte buffer for levels up to about 130, but for a larger level j passes 256 and that size argument becomes negative converted to size_t, so the writes go past the end of the buffer). If header is non-NULL it writes delimiters followed by 'header:value' and a newline when value is also non-NULL, or by 'header' and a newline when value is NULL; if header is NULL nothing is written (the delimiters were still updated).
note: reviewer (round15) right: for large level j can exceed sizeof(delimiters) and snprintf is then called with a wrapped size (isst-display.c:97-99), so the 'truncated to 256 bytes' claim holds only up to about level 130; round-0 reviewer's level-1 point (one space, not level-1 pairs) was already in the old prose.

name: format_and_print
prose:
Precondition: outf is a writable stream, level >= 0; in JSON mode header must be non-NULL whenever value is non-NULL or level > 0 and a '{' entry is wanted (it is passed to printf %s). Postcondition (format_and_print, isst-display.c:112-167; returns void): if out_format_is_json() is false it calls format_and_print_txt and returns, leaving the static last_level unchanged. In JSON mode with level 0 it writes '{' if header is non-NULL or '
}
' if header is NULL. With level > 0 it builds an indentation of two spaces per level in the static delimiters buffer, writes ',
' if last_level equals level, and then: if value is non-NULL it writes a newline when last_level differs from level and then '<indent>"header": "value"'; if value is NULL it writes the closing '}' lines (with a trailing comma on the line for level when header is non-NULL) for the levels from last_level-1 down to level, a newline when |last_level - level| < 3, and, if header is non-NULL, '<indent>"header": {'. In every JSON-mode path (level 0 included) last_level is then set to level. As in the text variant, the snprintf-based indentation can write past the 256-byte delimiters buffer for very large levels.
note: reviewer (round15) right: in JSON mode a NULL header with a value is passed to printf '%s' (isst-display.c:143), so the old precondition (only outf and level) was incomplete; round-0 reviewer's text-mode last_level point was already in the old prose.

name: chacha_s390_test_init
prose: Precondition: called once at module load with no parameters; the module parameters data_size and debug are set. Postcondition (chacha_s390_test_init, test-cipher.c:236-352): it allocates the plain buffer with vmalloc and the cipher_generic, cipher_s390 and revert buffers with vzalloc (each data_size bytes), fills plain with 'a' and up to 256 random bytes, and runs the generic, s390 and library ChaCha20 encrypt/decrypt and comparison checks, logging their results with pr_info; a failed allocation, a nonzero result of test_skcipher or a failed comparison stops the checks and jumps to out (a failed allocation or comparison sets the local ret to -2, test_skcipher's nonzero result is stored in ret). The out label then vfree()s each of the four buffers that is non-NULL and the function returns -1 unconditionally: the local ret is not used in the return statement, so the result is -1 on every path, whether the checks passed or failed.
note: reviewer (round15) wrong: the final statement is 'return -1;' (test-cipher.c:351), not 'return ret', so -2 is never returned; the old prose's 'always returns -1' is correct. Contract left empty: the function uses module globals and allocates memory.

name: mock_clear_event
prose: Precondition: cmd->payload_in points to a readable struct cxl_mbox_clear_event_payload with nr_recs handles; dev identifies the mock device. Postcondition (mock_clear_event, mem.c:314-356): it returns -EINVAL, without modifying any log state, if pl->event_log is >= CXL_EVENT_TYPE_MAX. It looks up the mock log for that type; if there is none it returns 0 (success) without changing anything. Otherwise it returns -EINVAL, still without modifying the log, if log->clear_idx + pl->nr_recs exceeds log->cur_idx or if any of the nr_recs handles differs from the expected consecutive handle sequence starting at the log's current clear handle. If all checks pass it sets log->nr_overflow to 0 if it was nonzero, advances log->clear_idx by pl->nr_recs and returns 0.
note: reviewer (round15) right: a missing mock log is not rejected, it returns 0 (mem.c:325-327); the old precondition text said it was rejected although its postcondition already had the 0 return. Round-0 reviewer point covered.

name: mock_passphrase_secure_erase
prose: Precondition: mdata is the mock memdev state and cmd->payload_in holds a struct cxl_pass_erase when the sizes are right. Postcondition (mock_passphrase_secure_erase, mem.c:948-1044): it returns -EINVAL, leaving cmd->return_code unchanged, if cmd->size_in is not sizeof(struct cxl_pass_erase) or cmd->size_out is not 0. It returns -ENXIO with cmd->return_code = CXL_MBOX_CMD_RC_SECURITY if the security state is frozen, or if USER_PLIMIT is set and the type is user, or if MASTER_PLIMIT is set and the type is master. For a master erase: if MASTER_PASS_SET is clear it returns -EINVAL (return_code unchanged); if the supplied passphrase differs from master_pass it calls master_plimit_check, sets return_code to CXL_MBOX_CMD_RC_PASSPHRASE and returns -ENXIO; if it matches it sets master_limit and user_limit to 0, clears USER_PASS_SET, zeroes user_pass, clears LOCKED, and returns 0 (master_pass and MASTER_PASS_SET are unchanged). For a user erase: if USER_PASS_SET is set and the passphrase differs from user_pass it calls user_plimit_check, sets return_code to CXL_MBOX_CMD_RC_PASSPHRASE and returns -ENXIO; if USER_PASS_SET is set and the passphrase matches it sets user_limit to 0, clears USER_PASS_SET and zeroes user_pass and returns 0 (LOCKED and master state unchanged); if USER_PASS_SET is clear it changes nothing and returns 0. Any other erase type returns -EINVAL with return_code unchanged by this function.
note: reviewer (round15) wrong at this function level: the default case simply returns -EINVAL (mem.c:1039-1040) and nothing here assigns CXL_MBOX_CMD_RC_INPUT, so return_code is not modified by this function (a caller may set it elsewhere); also added the user-erase-without-USER_PASS_SET path, which returns 0 with no change.

name: nfit_test_watermark(x)
prose:
Generated function x##_test (defined by the macro nfit_test_watermark(x), watermark.h:17-23; for example pmem_test, libnvdimm_test, acpi_nfit_test). Precondition: none; the generated function takes no arguments. Postcondition: it calls pr_debug with the format '%s for nfit_test
' and KBUILD_MODNAME (the message appears only if debug printing is enabled for that call site) and returns 0. The same macro also expands to EXPORT_SYMBOL(x##_test), which exports the generated function; that is not part of the function's run-time behavior.
note: reviewer (round15) concern was only about the formal contract omitting side effects; contract left empty (the function emits a debug message). Name set to the macro definition head per method rule 5.

name: DEF_INST_RAISE_SIG(sigill, SIGILL)
prose: Generated function inst_raise_sigill(hwcap, have_hwcap) (from DEF_INST_RAISE_SIG(sigill, SIGILL), hwcap.c:1221-1255, instantiated at line 1257). Precondition: hwcap points to a valid hwcap_data with a name string; have_hwcap says whether the CPU advertises the extension. Postcondition: if hwcap->sigill_fn is NULL it reports a skipped test and returns true without installing a handler or running anything. Otherwise it calls install_sigaction(SIGILL, handle_sigill) (the process exits through ksft_exit_fail_msg if sigaction fails), clears seen_sigill, calls hwcap->sigill_fn(), and reports the result: when have_hwcap is true it passes if no SIGILL was seen; when have_hwcap is false and hwcap->sigill_reliable is true it passes if SIGILL was seen; otherwise it prints whether SIGILL was reported and reports a skip. It then calls uninstall_sigaction(SIGILL), which only calls sigaction(SIGILL, NULL, NULL) (a query that leaves the installed handler in place; the process exits through ksft_exit_fail_msg if that call fails), and returns seen_sigill, i.e. true if SIGILL was seen.
note: reviewer (round15) right: uninstall_sigaction (hwcap.c:1214-1219) calls sigaction(signum, NULL, NULL), which does not change the disposition, so the old 'uninstalls the handler' was false; round-0 reviewer's skip-path point (returns true without installing/running) was already in the old prose. Named by the macro invocation per method rule 5.

name: DEF_INST_RAISE_SIG(sigbus, SIGBUS)
prose: Generated function inst_raise_sigbus(hwcap, have_hwcap) (from DEF_INST_RAISE_SIG(sigbus, SIGBUS), hwcap.c:1221-1255, instantiated at line 1258). Precondition: hwcap points to a valid hwcap_data with a name string; have_hwcap says whether the CPU advertises the extension. Postcondition: if hwcap->sigbus_fn is NULL it reports a skipped test and returns true without installing a handler or running anything. Otherwise it calls install_sigaction(SIGBUS, handle_sigbus) (the process exits through ksft_exit_fail_msg if sigaction fails), clears seen_sigbus, calls hwcap->sigbus_fn(), and reports the result: when have_hwcap is true it passes if no SIGBUS was seen; when have_hwcap is false and hwcap->sigbus_reliable is true it passes if SIGBUS was seen; otherwise it prints whether SIGBUS was reported and reports a skip. It then calls uninstall_sigaction(SIGBUS), which only calls sigaction(SIGBUS, NULL, NULL) (a query that leaves the installed handler in place; the process exits through ksft_exit_fail_msg if that call fails), and returns seen_sigbus, i.e. true if SIGBUS was seen.
note: reviewer (round15) right: uninstall_sigaction (hwcap.c:1214-1219) calls sigaction(signum, NULL, NULL), which does not change the disposition, so the old 'uninstalls the handler' was false; round-0 reviewer's skip-path point (returns true without installing/running) was already in the old prose. Named by the macro invocation per method rule 5.

name: create_sockets
prose: Precondition: none; the function uses the global ctx (it does not touch ctx.skel). Postcondition (create_sockets, bench_sockmap.c:190-234): it creates a listening AF_INET stream socket in ctx.sfd (socket, SO_REUSEPORT, bind to the address from init_addr, listen) and then calls create_pair for (ctx.c1, ctx.p1) and (ctx.c2, ctx.p2). If socket() fails it prints a message and returns ctx.sfd (negative); if setsockopt, bind or listen fails it returns that call's nonzero result, leaving ctx.sfd open; if either create_pair returns nonzero it returns that value. Otherwise it prints the four descriptors and returns 0. create_pair (bench_sockmap.c:157-188) can itself return 0 without having set its outputs: its error returns use the variable err, which is still 0 when socket() fails (and when accept() fails after a successful connect), so create_sockets can return 0 while ctx.c1/p1 or ctx.c2/p2 keep their previous values; when connect failed with EINPROGRESS an accept() failure returns -1. In create_pair's failure paths its local client descriptor is not stored in ctx and is not closed.
note: reviewer mixed: round-1 reviewer wrong (create_pair does return err=0 on socket() failure, bench_sockmap.c:168-171); round-15 right that accept() failure can return -1 (when connect returned -1/EINPROGRESS) and that cfd leaks (not stored in ctx, never closed) so 'descriptors already created remain open for the caller to clean up' is not true for it.

name: bpf_in_interrupt
prose: Precondition: none for compilation, but the header documents that it only works on x86 and arm64; it is meant to be called from BPF programs. Postcondition (bpf_in_interrupt, bpf_experimental.h:642-654): it reads pcnt = get_preempt_count(), which is the current CPU's __preempt_count on x86, the current task's thread_info.preempt.count on arm64, and 0 on any other architecture. When the kconfig value CONFIG_PREEMPT_RT is false it returns pcnt & (NMI_MASK | HARDIRQ_MASK | SOFTIRQ_MASK). When CONFIG_PREEMPT_RT is true it returns (pcnt & (NMI_MASK | HARDIRQ_MASK)) | (softirq_disable_cnt of the current task & SOFTIRQ_MASK), where the current task comes from bpf_get_current_task_btf. The result is 0 exactly when all bits selected by the applicable expression are 0. On architectures other than x86 and arm64 the preempt count part is always 0, so the function does not report hardirq/NMI/softirq state there (with PREEMPT_RT it can still return the softirq bits). It takes no locks and allocates nothing.
note: reviewer (round15) right that the old 'may be called on any architecture' was misleading: the header comment (bpf_experimental.h:637-641) says it only works on x86 and arm64; round-2 reviewer's PREEMPT_RT point is stated explicitly. Contract left empty (reads per-cpu/task state).

name: create_lru_hash
prose: Precondition: type and map_flags are passed through unchanged to the map creation; they are not validated by this helper. Postcondition (create_lru_hash, map_percpu_stats.c:385-390): it calls map_create(type, "lru_hash", opts) with map options carrying map_flags; map_create_opts then creates a BPF map with bpf_map_create using int-sized (4-byte) key and value, max_entries MAX_ENTRIES (16384), or MAX_ENTRIES_HASH_OF_MAPS (64) when type is BPF_MAP_TYPE_HASH_OF_MAPS. If bpf_map_create returns a negative value the CHECK macro prints a failure message and terminates the process with exit(-1), so the function does not return a negative value; on success it returns the new map file descriptor, which the caller owns.
note: reviewer concerns (rounds 1/2/15) were about the formal contract only; contract left empty. Old prose said 'returns -1 if creation fails (errno set)', but map_create_opts (map_percpu_stats.c:349-353) uses CHECK from test_maps.h which calls exit(-1) on failure.

name: csum_fold
prose: Precondition: none; csum may be any 32-bit unsigned value. Postcondition: returns the 16-bit one's complement of the twice-folded sum, i.e. 65535 minus b where a = (csum & 0xffff) + (csum >> 16) and b = (a & 0xffff) + (a >> 16); the function has no side effects.
note: re-checked against network_helpers.h:122-128: two folds of the low and high 16 bits leave a value <= 0xffff (max 0xfffe + 1), so (__u16)~csum equals 65535 minus it; prose and contract unchanged. Reviewer (rounds 2/15) wrong: a pure function's contract does not need to state 'no side effects'.

name: test_bpf_nf_ct_fail_tests
note: not a function: the slice (bpf_nf.c:10-22) holds the static data array test_bpf_nf_fail_tests (prog_name/err_msg pairs); no function of the packet name exists

name: bpf_prog_get_map_ids
prose: Precondition: prog_fd is a BPF program file descriptor, nr_map_ids points to a __u32 holding the capacity of the map_ids array, and map_ids is NULL or points to at least *nr_map_ids writable __u32 entries (the kernel writes into it only when the requested count is nonzero). Postcondition (bpf_prog_get_map_ids, fd_array.c:79-96): it zeroes a local bpf_prog_info, sets its nr_map_ids to *nr_map_ids and its map_ids pointer, and calls bpf_prog_get_info_by_fd. If that call returns nonzero it records an ASSERT_OK failure (the test is not aborted), returns -1 and leaves *nr_map_ids unchanged (map_ids may have been partly written by the kernel). Otherwise it stores in *nr_map_ids the nr_map_ids reported by the kernel, which is the program's total used-map count (not limited to the requested capacity; the kernel sets it to used_map_cnt and copies at most min(requested, used_map_cnt) ids into map_ids), and returns 0. The caller keeps ownership of map_ids.
note: reviewer (round15) right: the kernel sets info.nr_map_ids to the total used_map_cnt and copies only min(requested, total) ids (kernel/bpf/syscall.c:5032-5034), so *nr_map_ids is the total count, not min(requested,total); the round-1 reviewer's claim (min) was wrong and the round-2 claim (actual count) right.

name: query_prog_cnt
prose: Precondition: cgroup_fd is a valid cgroup file descriptor usable for a BPF_LSM_CGROUP program query, and attach_func is either NULL or a NUL-terminated string naming a BTF FUNC symbol; the caller holds no locks that the function affects. Postcondition: the function returns a __u32: when attach_func is NULL it returns the program count reported by bpf_prog_query_opts (0 if that query failed, since the options struct is zero-initialized); when attach_func is non-NULL it returns (__u32)-1 (4294967295) if the vmlinux BTF cannot be loaded, and otherwise returns the number of attached programs whose attach_btf_id equals the BTF id of attach_func (if the symbol is not found btf__find_by_name_kind returns a negative value, which as an unsigned comparison does not match a real attach_btf_id, so the count is normally 0); failed ASSERT_* checks only record a test failure and do not abort, so the function always continues and returns one of these values; it allocates and frees its own temporary prog_ids/prog_attach_flags buffers, may cache the vmlinux BTF handle in the file-static btf for later calls, and hands the caller no new memory or references.
note: re-checked against lsm_cgroup.c:15-59. Reviewer (round15) wrong: the function is declared 'static __u32', so its 'return -1' is the value 4294967295 as the prose says; rounds 1/2 points (ASSERT_* do not abort) already in the prose. Wording about a not-found symbol tightened.

name: run_test
prose: Precondition: cgroup_fd is an open cgroup directory descriptor, server_fd an open listening socket descriptor, and is_mptcp selects the MPTCP verification (verify_msk) instead of the plain TCP one (verify_tsk). Postcondition (run_test, mptcp.c:156-189): it loads the mptcp_sock skeleton; if that fails it returns libbpf_get_error() of the skeleton pointer (a negative value) without anything to destroy. Otherwise it attaches the skeleton; if that fails err (the attach error) is returned after destroying the skeleton. It attaches the sockops program to cgroup_fd (a nonzero result is returned after destroying the skeleton; the program is not detached on later paths) and connects to server_fd; if connect_to_fd fails it returns -EIO after destroying the skeleton (no client descriptor to close). On a successful connect it returns the result of the verification function, then closes the client descriptor and destroys the skeleton: verify_tsk returns the bpf_map_lookup_elem error if the lookup fails, else the number of failed checks (0 to 2); verify_msk returns -1 if the skeleton's token is not positive, the lookup error if the lookup fails, else the number of failed checks (0 to 5). So the result is 0 when everything passes, a positive failed-check count when verification assertions fail, and a negative value for setup, connect or lookup failures. Failed ASSERT_* checks only record a failure and do not abort the function.
note: reviewer concerns: round-0 reviewer (verification failures return positive err) right and already in the old prose; rounds 2/15 only about the formal contract, which is left empty. Rewritten to add the verify_msk token check (-1) and the lookup-error returns (mptcp.c:123-153, 90-101).

name: run_test
prose: Precondition: cgroup_fd is an open cgroup descriptor, test points to an initialized struct sockopt_test (the function may rewrite test->set_optlen and test->get_optlen), use_io_uring selects io_uring for the set/get calls and use_link selects bpf_link_create instead of bpf_prog_attach. Postcondition (run_test, sockopt.c:1071-1196): it loads the test's BPF program; if the load fails it returns 0 when test->error is DENY_LOAD, otherwise -1 (nothing to clean up). It attaches the program (by link or by prog attach); on failure it returns 0 when test->error is DENY_ATTACH, otherwise -1, after closing the program fd. It then creates an AF_INET stream socket (failure: -1, after detaching or closing the link and closing the program fd). If set_optlen is nonzero (first rescaled: lengths of at least PAGE_SIZE become (n / PAGE_SIZE) * sysconf(_SC_PAGESIZE) + n % PAGE_SIZE) it calls setsockopt; a failure with errno EPERM and test->error EPERM_SETSOCKOPT, or EFAULT and EFAULT_SETSOCKOPT, ends the test with 0; any other failure returns -1. If get_optlen is nonzero (rescaled the same way) it allocates a zeroed optval buffer (malloc result unchecked) and calls getsockopt; a failure with EOPNOTSUPP, EPERM or EFAULT matching EOPNOTSUPP_GETSOCKOPT, EPERM_GETSOCKOPT or EFAULT_GETSOCKOPT ends the test with 0, any other failure returns -1, and a returned optlen different from the expected one (get_optlen_ret, or get_optlen) or a returned optval different from test->get_optval also returns -1. If no operation ended the test earlier it returns (test->error != OK): 0 when no error was expected, 1 when an error was expected but did not occur. Every path after the attach frees optval if allocated, closes the socket if created, closes the link or detaches the program, and closes the program fd; the caller keeps cgroup_fd and test.
note: reviewer (round15) mostly wrong: the old prose already listed the optlen/optval mismatch among the -1 returns; kept the substance but clarified it and added the use_io_uring/use_link parameters it omitted. Round-2 reviewer's page-size rescaling point was already right in the old prose.

name: test_sockopt_sk
prose: Precondition: called by the test_progs harness with no arguments (the function returns void). Postcondition (test_sockopt_sk, sockopt_sk.c:249-259): it calls test__join_cgroup("/sockopt_sk"). If the returned descriptor is negative, ASSERT_GE records a failure and the function returns without running anything. Otherwise it calls run_test(cgroup_fd) and then closes cgroup_fd. It returns no value.
note: slice cut the head; real function test_sockopt_sk (sockopt_sk.c:249). Old prose re-checked and kept in substance.

name: test_test_local_storage
prose: Precondition: called by the test_progs harness with no arguments (returns void); needs a working BPF LSM environment, /bin/rm, cp, mv and rm. Postcondition (test_test_local_storage, test_local_storage.c:91-172): it loads and attaches the local_storage skeleton, opens a pidfd for the current process and runs check_syscall_operations on task_storage_map; it creates a temporary directory with mkdtemp, copies /bin/rm into it with system(cp), opens the copy and runs check_syscall_operations on inode_storage_map; it runs run_self_unlink and expects EPERM; it sets monitored_pid to the current pid, renames the copy with system(mv) and checks inode_storage_result is 0, starts an AF_INET6 stream server, checks sk_storage_result is 0 and runs check_syscall_operations on sk_storage_map. A failed ASSERT jumps out of the sequence for these steps: skeleton load, attach, pidfd_open, the task-storage check and mkdtemp jump to close_prog (no directory exists or is removed); system(cp), the open of the copy, the inode-storage check, run_self_unlink, system(mv), start_server and the sk-storage check jump to close_prog_rmdir. The two ASSERT_EQ checks on inode_storage_result and sk_storage_result only record failures and do not jump. close_prog_rmdir runs 'rm -rf' on the temporary directory (it is also reached by falling through at the end of a successful run); close_prog then closes serv_sk, rm_fd and task_fd (possibly still -1) and destroys the skeleton (possibly NULL).
note: reviewer (round15) right: the system("mv") assertion (test_local_storage.c:149-150) also jumps to close_prog_rmdir and was missing from the old list; round-1 and round-2 points (mv should succeed; cleanup via close_prog skips rm -rf) were already reflected in the old prose.

name: test_xdp_metadata
prose: Precondition: called by the test_progs harness with no arguments (returns void); needs permission to create network namespaces, a veth pair and XSK sockets, and the xdp_metadata and xdp_metadata2 skeletons. Postcondition (test_xdp_metadata, xdp_metadata.c:349-545): it creates a TX and an RX network namespace with a veth pair (plus a VLAN interface and a static neighbor entry), opens an AF_XDP socket on the RX interface, opens and loads the xdp_metadata skeleton with the 'rx' and 'redirect' programs bound to the RX interface, checks that the dev-bound program cannot be added to a program array or a devmap, attaches the XDP program, registers the XSK socket in the xsk map, opens an AF_XDP socket on the TX side and sends packets (from AF_XDP and from the network stack) whose metadata is verified on the RX side with verify_xsk_metadata, then loads and attaches the xdp_metadata2 'freplace_rx' program targeting 'rx', sends one more packet and asserts that its 'called' counter is greater than 0. Each step is checked with an ASSERT_* or SYS macro; on any failed check execution jumps to out and the remaining steps are skipped. The out label always (success or failure) closes both XSK sockets, destroys both skeletons (a NULL skeleton is tolerated), closes the namespace token if one is open and runs 'ip netns del' on both namespaces, ignoring failures. The polling loop 'while (!retries--)' with retries starting at 10 does not execute its body (the condition is false on entry), so the 'called' counter is read once, immediately.
note: slice cut the head; real function test_xdp_metadata (xdp_metadata.c:349). Old prose re-checked; added the retries-loop observation (xdp_metadata.c:529-533) and the exact cleanup set.

name: arena_spin_lock_irqsave
note: not a function: function-like statement-expression macro (bpf_arena_spin_lock.h:524-532) wrapping bpf_local_irq_save, arena_spin_lock and a conditional bpf_local_irq_restore; no function of this name is defined

name: arena_spin_unlock_irqrestore
note: not a function: function-like statement-expression macro (bpf_arena_spin_lock.h:534-538) that only forwards to arena_spin_unlock and bpf_local_irq_restore

name: cubic_root
prose: Precondition: none; a may be any 64-bit unsigned value. Postcondition (cubic_root, bpf_cubic.c:239-267): the function is pure and returns an approximation (average error about 0.2%, per the source comment) of the cube root of a as a __u32. For a < 64 it returns (v[a] + 35) >> 6 from the 64-entry table v, which gives 0 for a = 0 and a value of at least 1 for every a from 1 to 63. For a >= 64 it computes b from the bit length of a, shift = a >> (3 * b), returns 0 if shift >= 64 (a bound check for the verifier; with b = (bit_length * 84 >> 8) - 1 the shift stays below 64 for every 64-bit a, including the extremes 2^k - 1 that I tried), and otherwise starts from x = ((v[shift] + 10) << b) >> 6 and applies one Newton-Raphson step x = (2 * x + a / (x * (x - 1))) followed by x = (x * 341) >> 10, returning x. No locks, references or memory are involved.
note: reviewer (round1/2/15) concerns were about older contracts (result <= a, missing no-side-effect clause); the old numeric bound 'result <= 4194304' is dropped because the code gives no proof of it (I computed the algorithm for 2^64-1: 2641850 and for 64: 4). Contract left empty. Checked numerically that every tested nonzero a gives a nonzero result.

name: bictcp_update
prose: Precondition: ca points to a valid bpf_bictcp state, cwnd is the current congestion window in packets and acked the number of newly acknowledged packets. Postcondition (bictcp_update, bpf_cubic.c:272-383; returns void): it first adds acked to ca->ack_cnt. If ca->last_cwnd equals cwnd and the signed difference tcp_jiffies32 - ca->last_time is at most HZ/32 it returns, having changed only ack_cnt (ca->cnt keeps its old value). Otherwise, if ca->epoch_start is nonzero and tcp_jiffies32 equals ca->last_time it skips directly to the TCP-friendliness step without recalculating the cubic state or ca->cnt; if not, it sets ca->last_cwnd and ca->last_time, and when ca->epoch_start is 0 it starts a new epoch: epoch_start = tcp_jiffies32, ack_cnt = acked, tcp_cwnd = cwnd, and bic_K and bic_origin_point are set (K = 0 and origin = cwnd if last_max_cwnd <= cwnd, otherwise K from cubic_root of cube_factor * (last_max_cwnd - cwnd) and origin = last_max_cwnd). It then computes the cubic target from the elapsed time and sets ca->cnt to cwnd / (bic_target - cwnd) when bic_target > cwnd or to 100 * cwnd otherwise, capped at 20 when last_max_cwnd is 0. If tcp_friendliness is on, it updates ca->tcp_cwnd and reduces ca->ack_cnt by the whole multiples of the window-based delta, and if ca->tcp_cwnd exceeds cwnd it lowers ca->cnt to cwnd / (tcp_cwnd - cwnd) when that is smaller. On every path that gets past the early return it finally sets ca->cnt to max(ca->cnt, 2).
note: reviewer (round15) right: a new epoch also sets ca->tcp_cwnd = cwnd (bpf_cubic.c:296); the round-0 reviewer's early-return point was already covered in the old prose. Added that ack_cnt can also be reduced in the TCP-friendly step.

name: CHECK(map, push_back, &v->head, &f->node2)
prose: Generated function map_missing_lock_push_back(ctx) (from CHECK(map, push_back, &v->head, &f->node2), linked_list_fail.c:71-78 and 87). The program is a verifier-negative test (SEC("?tc"), optional load): it is meant to be rejected by the BPF verifier and is not expected to run. The INIT macro at its start looks up map_of_maps, array_map (twice) and the inner map (twice) and allocates three objects with bpf_obj_new, returning 0 at once (dropping any objects already allocated) if any step fails. If it gets past INIT it calls bpf_list_push_back(&v->head, &f->node2) on the list head in the array-map value without taking the spin lock that protects it, and returns 0. It takes and releases no lock; the kfunc call would hand the ownership of the object containing f->node2 to the list, and the program drops neither the other two allocated objects nor holds any lock, which is what the verifier is expected to reject. Returns 0 on every path that returns.

name: kprobe_ret__do_filp_open
prose: Precondition: ctx is the pt_regs of the return from do_filp_open, whose return value is a struct file pointer or an error pointer; no allowlist state or data_heap scratch slot has to exist beforehand. Postcondition (kprobe_ret__do_filp_open, profiler.inc.h:755-815; slice cut the head, and the packet name kprobe__vfs_open is not a function in the file): it records function statistics on entry and exit, and returns 0 on every path. It emits nothing when the returned file pointer is NULL or an error pointer, when the file's open flags include neither O_RDWR nor O_WRONLY, when O_TMPFILE is set, when the file's inode mode is a directory, character device, block device, FIFO or socket, when is_dentry_allowed_for_filemod rejects the dentry, or when the data_heap scratch slot cannot be looked up. Otherwise it fills the slot with a FILEMOD_EVENT of fmod_type FMOD_OPEN with the open flags in dst_flags, the file's inode and device id as destination, and zero source inode, device id and path length; it appends the process metadata, the cgroup information and the absolute destination file path (read_absolute_file_path_from_dentry) after the fixed fields, recording dst_filepath_length only when the path length is at most MAX_FILEPATH_LENGTH (otherwise the path is not counted and the length stays 0); it then sends the event to the events perf buffer with a length of the bytes filled, capped at sizeof(*filemod_data). It acquires no locks or references.
note: slice cut the head; real function kprobe_ret__do_filp_open (the packet prose describes this return probe, not a vfs_open kprobe). Old prose said it fires for any open flags and that the dentry filter was the only gate; the flag, O_TMPFILE and inode-type filters were missing (profiler.inc.h:762-773).

name: cls_redirect
prose: Precondition: skb is the packet being processed by this tc program. Postcondition (cls_redirect, test_cls_redirect.c:933-1076; slice cut the head, process_gue_packet is not a function in the file): it returns TC_ACT_SHOT if the global metrics cannot be fetched; otherwise it increments processed_packets_total. It returns TC_ACT_OK (no further counters) when the packet is not IPv4, when bpf_skb_pull_data fails, when the encapsulation headers cannot be obtained, when the IP header has options (ihl != 5), when the destination address is not ENCAPSULATION_IP or the protocol is not UDP, or when the UDP destination port is not ENCAPSULATION_PORT. For packets addressed to the encapsulation endpoint it returns TC_ACT_SHOT after incrementing errors_total_fragmented_ip for a fragment, or errors_total_malformed_encapsulation for a nonzero GUE variant, control or flags, a GUE header length that does not match the hop count, or a nonzero unigue version; it returns TC_ACT_SHOT without a counter if unigue.reserved is nonzero. It then calls get_next_hop and returns its value unchanged if it is not CONTINUE_PROCESSING. If the next hop address is zero it increments accepted_packets_total_last_hop and returns accept_locally's result. Otherwise it dispatches on the GUE inner protocol: IPIP to process_ipv4, IPV6 to process_ipv6, any other value increments errors_total_unknown_l3_proto and returns TC_ACT_SHOT. For the verdict: INVALID returns TC_ACT_SHOT (the counters were already updated inside process_ipv4/6); UNKNOWN returns forward_to_next_hop's result; SYN with unigue.forward_syn set returns forward_to_next_hop's result; ECHO_REQUEST, SYN (with forward_syn clear), SYN_COOKIE and ESTABLISHED increment the matching accepted_packets_total_* counter and then return accept_locally's result.
note: slice cut the head; real function cls_redirect (test_cls_redirect.c:933). The old prose covered only the tail from the unigue.reserved check on; rewritten from the whole function.

name: csum_tcpudp_nofold
prose: Precondition: none for the result to be defined; on a little-endian build len + proto should not exceed 16777215 so that (proto + len) << 8 does not wrap in 32 bits. Postcondition (csum_tcpudp_nofold, test_tcp_custom_syncookie.h:53-66): the function is pure. It forms the 64-bit sum S = sum + saddr + daddr plus the pseudo-header term, which is proto + len when __BIG_ENDIAN is defined and (proto + len) << 8 (computed in 32-bit arithmetic) otherwise, and returns from64to32(S): x1 = (S mod 2^32) + floor(S / 2^32), x2 = (x1 mod 2^32) + floor(x1 / 2^32), result = x2 mod 2^32 (the two-step end-around-carry fold to 32 bits). It has no side effects.
note: reviewer (round15) right: the contract/old prose assumed the little-endian (len + proto) << 8 term; on __BIG_ENDIAN the code adds proto + len (lines 60-64). Contract left empty because it would be endian-specific.

name: verify_sleepable_user_copy
prose: Precondition: the function is inlined into a sleepable uprobe.session BPF program so that bpf_copy_from_user may be used; the global user_ptr is a user-space address. Postcondition (verify_sleepable_user_copy, uprobe_multi_session.c:57-63): it calls bpf_copy_from_user(data, 9, user_ptr) into the 9-byte local buffer data and ignores its return value; the kernel helper zero-fills the whole destination when the copy fails or is partial, so after a failed copy data holds 9 zero bytes. It then returns true exactly when bpf_strncmp(data, 9, "test_data") == 0, i.e. when the 9 bytes in data equal the 9 characters 'test_data'; it returns false in every other case, including after a failed copy (zeroed buffer). The buffer is local and not visible to the caller, and no locks or references are taken.
note: reviewer (round15) right: bpf_copy_from_user memsets the destination to 0 on failure (kernel/bpf/helpers.c:658-666), so the buffer is not left indeterminate; round-2's point that the return value is ignored was already correct. Contract left empty.

name: check_cookie
prose: Precondition: the globals idx_entry and idx_return are nonnegative and bpf_session_cookie() returns a valid pointer to the session cookie. Postcondition: the function returns 0 or 1; in a return session it returns 1 without changing either counter when idx_return >= 3, otherwise it stores the cookie into test_uprobe_cookie_return[idx_return], increments idx_return by one, leaves idx_entry unchanged and returns 0; in an entry session it returns 1 without changing either counter when idx_entry >= 6, otherwise it writes test_uprobe_cookie_entry[idx_entry] into the cookie, returns idx_entry % 2 (0 when idx_entry is even, 1 when odd) and increments idx_entry by one, leaving idx_return unchanged.
note: re-checked against uprobe_multi_session_recursive.c:19-34: prose matches the code. Contract dropped (it reads and writes globals idx_entry/idx_return and the cookie arrays, which method rule 4 excludes); the reviewers' points (rounds 0/2/15) concerned the formal contract, not the prose.
